reference: The request flows from the client to the FastAPI API, then to the retrieval/inference services as applicable, with Ollama and Code Llama producing the final answer.
retrieve.py is responsible for semantic retrieval and the retrieve(query) function performs the retrieval.
app.py contains the /ask-services endpoint.
create_embeddings.py generates embeddings and writes them to knowledge_base/embeddings.json. retrieve.py loads the embeddings and performs retrieval.
app.py calls the retrieval service through its /retrieve endpoint using RETRIEVAL_SERVICE_URL and receives retrieved context before calling the inference service.
retrieval_service.py imports the retrieve function from retrieve.py and calls retrieve(query) when its /retrieve endpoint is requested.
inference_service.py sends the prompt and model information to Ollama through its HTTP API at the Ollama generate endpoint.
The application loads knowledge_base/embeddings.json during startup. If the file is missing, loading the embeddings will fail and the application may fail to start.
If RETRIEVAL_SERVICE_URL points to the wrong port, app.py cannot successfully connect to the retrieval service, so the request will fail before getting retrieval context.
app.py expects the retrieval response to contain context. If context is missing, accessing or using that field can cause an error and prevent successful answer generation.
A valid FastAPI health endpoint should return a simple health/status response, for example @app.get('/health') followed by a function returning {'status':'healthy'}.
Cosine similarity should calculate dot product divided by the product of the two vector norms, with appropriate handling for zero norms.
The function should identify the index of the maximum similarity score and return the corresponding document.
Move common retrieval logic into a single reusable function/module and have app.py and the retrieval service use that shared implementation instead of duplicating retrieval code.
Move hard-coded inference configuration such as model name, num_predict, temperature, and URLs into configuration variables or environment variables.
Create reusable HTTP/client helper functions, centralize service URLs and timeout settings, and add consistent error handling instead of duplicating request logic inside the endpoint.
KEDA uses the Redis request queue length as the external event metric to scale inference worker pods.
Separating API pods from inference workers allows independent scaling and lets requests wait in Redis when workers are busy.
The flow is Client/User Request -> FastAPI API -> Redis Queue -> Inference Worker -> Ollama -> Code Llama -> Result.
